'''Brandon Ray Stokley''' (born June 23, 1976) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for fifteen seasons. Nicknamed "The Slot Machine," Stokley played [[college football]] for the [[Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns football|Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns]] and was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the fourth round of the [[1999 NFL draft]].

Stokley also played for the [[Indianapolis Colts]], [[Seattle Seahawks]], [[New York Giants]], and [[Denver Broncos]], earning two [[Super Bowl]] wins during his playing career. After retiring from the NFL, he became a radio personality.

He is currently Director of Mergers and Acquisitions at Round Hill Capital in London and a member of the Pennsylvania State University's board of trustees.

'''Brandon Joseph Winey''' (born January 27, 1978) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Washington Redskins]] and [[New York Giants]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]] and was selected by the [[Miami Dolphins]] in the sixth round of the [[2001 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2001 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2001/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Winey attended [[Washington-Marion Magnet High School]] in [[Lake Charles, Louisiana]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Brandon Winey NFL Football Statistics|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WineBr20.htm|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|accessdate=April 22, 2016}}</ref> 
On April 12, 2014, Winey was arrested for the shooting of LSU player Tahj Jones after an argument.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegefootball/eye-on-college-football/24523655/former-lsu-lb-tajh-jones-in-serious-condition-after-shooting |title=Former LSU LB Tahj Jones in serious condition after shooting |access-date=2014-04-12 |archive-date=2014-04-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140413124104/http://www.cbssports.com/collegefootball/eye-on-college-football/24523655/former-lsu-lb-tajh-jones-in-serious-condition-after-shooting |url-status=dead }}</ref> In January 2015, a grand jury declined to indict Winey.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/12139980/grand-jury-declines-indict-brandon-winey-former-lsu-tigers-player-shooting | title=Brandon Winey not indicted by jury | work=espn.com | date=January 8, 2015 | accessdate=24 August 2024}}</ref>
